title: Ailean set to the counting-house at Cathair dhearg
summary: Ailean mac Iain is set to the humans' counting-house at Cathair dhearg to box the north wall's tithe rolls unread, and says nothing of the letters a Mission reader taught him as a boy, for a clerk who reads aloud what he is told only to box is not a clerk kept long.

title: The fire-damaged tithe rolls boxed as loose leaves
summary: Where the counting-house fire at Cathair dhearg burned a shelf's ledgers through the middle rather than whole, Ailean gathers the crumbling leaves as best their order can be guessed and marks the crate that the order is his own guess and not to be trusted past that.

title: The Ros dhomhain tariff copied into Dia-thìris
summary: At the harbour offices of Ros dhomhain, Ailean copies the humans' tariff tables clause by clause into Dia-thìris, building the words for duties his own tongue had never before had cause to name, and the duty itself stands unchanged under its new ink.

title: The district surveys found behind a locked grating
summary: In the whole counting-house at Seann Skell in the west, Ailean forces a locked grating and finds eleven rolled district surveys, the only whole survey of the island's fields anywhere to be had, each walked, measured and scaled by the humans' own hand.

title: The surveys boxed apart and labelled for the council
summary: Ruairidh orders the district surveys boxed apart from the tithe rolls, for the council's own clerks rather than the reckoners, and Ailean chalks the crate's lid with six words rather than a description: the shires will be drawn on them.

title: The harbour store's lock broken at Ceann mhòr
summary: A fisherman of Ceann mhòr breaks the lock of the humans' harbour store with a hammer and stands back to let the town see what is inside, and it is the town, not the man who struck the lock, that shares the rope, canvas and salt out house by house within the hour.

title: The unfished nets loosed at Cathair gheal
summary: A whole loft of nets that had never been fished goes out to every boat in the harbour at Cathair gheal on a single tide, and the fleet fishes that year with gear it never paid a coin for and never afterward wonders whose it had been.

title: The reckoning drawn up by three women of Inis àrsaidh
summary: At Inis àrsaidh, poorer and smaller than its neighbours, three women of the town draw up on the spot the reckoning of who has a boat and who has none, and so who needs rope or salt the more, with no office to do it and none afterward to say they did it wrong.

title: The north-west locks left unanswered
summary: No maor comes north to ask who struck the first lock at Ceann mhòr, Cathair gheal or Inis àrsaidh before the following spring, by which time there is nothing left locked to account for, and the towns' own telling of the broken stores hardens into the kind of story a place keeps because it likes its shape.

title: The mint's first seal cut at Cathair dhearg
summary: In the same week as the proclamation, the mint at Cathair dhearg begins cutting the state's first seal for its own coin and its own letters, to be set upon documents no different in kind from the ones Ailean spent the summer boxing unread.

title: Rìoghachd Dia-thìr proclaimed from the counting-house steps
summary: A herald reads the council's proclamation from the steps of the Cathair dhearg counting-house, naming the state Rìoghachd Dia-thìr and the years of settling complete; Ailean stands in the crowd and does not cheer, thinking the naming a kind of label, true as far as it goes and silent about the rest.

title: The proclamation read at the market crosses of the south
summary: Copies of the proclamation styling the state Rìoghachd Dia-thìr are read at the market crosses of every southern town within the fortnight, in the same flat, official voice, whatever crowd happens to be standing near enough to hear it.
